body:
## Feasibility and intended outcome

**Feasible as a continuously available intake/admission service over the existing machinery.** The LLM should wake for changed eligible material and propose logical grouping; deterministic contracts decide whether membership can change. A resident LLM thinking continuously is unnecessary. The difficult work is eligibility, freshness, and coordination, not polling GitHub.

**Hard requirement from the operator:** `bug report → GitHub issue → remediation plan included in that GitHub issue → eligibility checks → Jog/Marathon candidate`. **A GitHub issue that is only a bug report does not qualify**, even with high PRS ratings, a ready label, or a locally drafted checklist. The monitor may report `NEEDS-PLAN`; it must not draft the missing plan and approve its own admission.

This is an initial design sketch, not an approved implementation plan, active marathon, or authorization to dispatch/merge.

## What we can reuse, and what that actually proves

Source recon at `507286b333bc95caf7021edfc82d7f7add259c32`, 2026-09-08; links are pinned to that revision. Graph generation was stale, so material claims below were checked against source. No runtime experiment is claimed.

| Existing part | Reuse / boundary |
|---|---|
| [`10days` scanner](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/507286b333bc95caf7021edfc82d7f7add259c32/skills/10days/scan-issues.sh#L63) and skill | Already discovers recently updated open issues; the scanner caps at 200. Reuse the discovery idea, not the whole auto-fire workflow: `/10days` can author contracts and execute, which exceeds this monitor's contract. |
| [`marathon-triage`](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/507286b333bc95caf7021edfc82d7f7add259c32/skills/marathon-triage/SKILL.md) | Existing classification, write-set audit, preflight, and wave review procedure. Skills provide reasoning discipline; prose alone is not machine enforcement. |
| [Planner](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/507286b333bc95caf7021edfc82d7f7add259c32/utils/py/_marathon_plan.py#L760) | Already reads RELEASES DB and local capture docs; packs waves using dependencies, paths, and zone limits. Current scoring at L1038 still uses PDDA effort/complexity/risk, not verified PRS. |
| [Preflight](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/507286b333bc95caf7021edfc82d7f7add259c32/utils/py/swarm_preflight.py#L1430) | Validates contract, target, artifacts, probes and some issue acceptance. Local remediation source/criteria or a local Phase/checklist can satisfy its remediation check; it does not establish our required plan-in-GitHub gate. |
| [RELEASES/Jog writer](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/507286b333bc95caf7021edfc82d7f7add259c32/utils/py/releases_app.py#L3876) | Canonical CLI and receipt-backed writes already exist. `jog add` refuses pending/running duplicates but can reactivate terminal rows and reset attempts: automatic rescans must never do that. `jog to-marathon` at L4150 prints issue IDs, not a complete reviewed plan. |
| [Machine contracts](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/507286b333bc95caf7021edfc82d7f7add259c32/MACHINE-CONTRACTS.md) | Reuse `marathon-invocation@1` and `marathon-drive/result@1`. Marathon keeps execution/review/gate/PR ownership; Jog keeps queue and lease ownership. Admission is an upstream policy decision, not a new executor. |
| [`start-task` rating policy](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/507286b333bc95caf7021edfc82d7f7add259c32/skills/start-task/SKILL.md#L171) | Four 1–100 axes `pri/sev/appeal/effort`; effort means cheapness, appeal defaults to 50. Rank is sum unless operator `ovr` replaces it. Preserve overrides; do not invent another composite score or convert implementation risk into bug severity. |

## Proposed admission contract

All gates must pass. Missing, malformed, stale, conflicting, or unavailable evidence means **held**, with a named reason. Ranking never overrides a failed gate.

| Gate | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Issue identity | Allowlisted repository + stable issue identity; live OPEN issue; not duplicate, cancelled, already delivered, already claimed, or parked after failed attempts. PRs are separate delivery/conflict evidence, not issue candidates. |
| Remediation plan **in the issue** | Substantive plan in the issue body, or a specifically selected plan comment belonging to that issue. A label, placeholder heading, external link alone, local-only plan, or generic “fix and test” fails. Default proposal: body section; comment support requires an unambiguous selected comment ID. |
| Plan substance | Observed bug/repro and grounded diagnosis; bounded ordered remedy; affected paths/contracts; dependencies; measurable acceptance with meaningful red controls; test/gate commands; non-goals; risk and rollback. Recon/debug-mantra/workhorse can produce this upstream; the monitor consumes it. |
| Independent review | Trusted reviewer acceptance bound to the exact plan content hash/revision and applicable policy. An author-written `approved: true` or LLM confidence is insufficient. Specify reviewer identity and authority before implementing automatic admission. |
| PRS | All four valid axes and rationale included in the issue; canonical DB row agrees. Review/rating provenance refers to this plan revision; preserve operator appeal/priority/ovr. Generic row `updated_at` is not proof of rating review. |
| Local execution readiness | Matching PDDA capture/active doc and roadmap identity, current preflight contract, known target base SHA, meaningful probes, truthful effective write-set, and explicit independent builder/reviewer route. Auto-promotion, if needed, is a separately granted writer capability. |
| Scheduling safety | Dependencies exist and are satisfied or scheduled earlier; no cycles; effective paths and shared interfaces checked; zone/kernel caps, resource budget, release/umbrella identity, operator holds, and active claims respected. |
| Freshness and authority | Immediately before membership write, revalidate issue state, plan/review/rating hashes, target SHA, queue revision and policy version. Auto-inclusion requires an explicit repo policy; auto-start and auto-merge remain separate capabilities. |

Issue text, comments, and plan commands are untrusted input. Extract them as data; do not execute pasted shell commands merely to decide eligibility. Any probe execution goes through trusted existing preflight in a disposable full clone with its normal containment.

## Logical grouping

Use the LLM for explanations and semantic similarity, then validate its suggested groups mechanically.

- **Jog:** bounded, independently deliverable fixes that benefit from serial execution; overlapping work can be ordered after dependency review. A group can share a subsystem without claiming one root cause.
- **Marathon:** real repeated transform or coherent long arc, decomposable into lanes with machine-checkable per-item outcomes. Prove each member belongs; similar titles or high aggregate PRS do not establish cohesion. Disjoint files still may share a runtime contract.
- **Hold:** missing plan/review/rating, uncertain dependency, unsafe contract seam, policy-excluded risk, stale evidence, or no honest fit. A high-severity bug can rank urgently while its high-risk implementation still needs manual handling.

Preserve exactly one active long-horizon marathon. New candidates go into a future proposal; never silently append to/reorder the committed running wave. Selection of the next marathon remains a deliberate policy/operator decision. Idle is valid; do not manufacture load. Keep issue-level scores visible rather than hiding them behind a group sum.

## Smallest useful architecture and missing pieces

`updated issue → deterministic cheap filters → plan/review/PRS validation → bounded LLM grouping → deterministic admission checks → reviewable proposal → authorized membership write`

After Phase 0, start with an outbound-only periodic one-shot process once an hour under the existing local scheduler if suitable. It needs a UTC cursor with overlap, complete pagination, dedupe, retry/backoff and a periodic reconciliation sweep for closures/reopens/edits. The REST issues endpoint can also return PRs, so filter them explicitly. [GitHub API reference](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues?apiVersion=latest), [pagination](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).

Missing pieces to implement or verify:

- A versioned issue-plan/review/rating admission envelope and reason codes, with hashes and immutable source references. GitHub remains the discussion/plan publication surface; PROJECT is the execution surface; RELEASES owns ratings/membership. Synchronization must detect disagreement, not select a convenient copy.
- A strict admission validator reused by monitor and queue insertion. Current planner output is advisory: source inspection found unmapped deep-preflight failures (L985–1007), advisory missing dependencies (L1010–1027), and a no-progress wave fallback (L1114–1119). Reproduce these paths before specifying fixes; all nonzero/unknown results must hold automatic admission.
- One effective write-set shared between grouping and execution. Planner uses declared artifacts (L657–671); preflight expands tests/helpers (L1259). Validate each member's complete packet rather than assuming one bundled primary plan proves all members.
- Crash-safe, idempotent membership reservation through canonical writers. Bind to repo/issue + plan/review revision; enforce queue revision checks under the writer lock. Coordinate across clones, not just one clone's driver lock. A repeat scan must never reset a parked item's attempt cap or create a second active membership.
- Durable decision receipts: inputs/hashes, model/policy versions, reason, proposal, and writer result; dashboard/report exposes candidates **and exclusions**. Cursor/cache is derived ingestion state, not a second work ledger.
- Budget/liveness controls: one scan lease, model calls only on changed content, bounded tokens/time/retries (initial proposal: two model attempts per revision), API backoff, actionable error/last-success reporting, and kill switch. Budget exhaustion holds work; it never weakens gates. Operator drops persist until deliberately released.

## Candidate model and Phase 0 technical spike

**Candidate: GPT-5.6 Luna (`gpt-5.6-luna`) as the initial hourly intake orchestrator.** This is a candidate to evaluate, not a proven model assignment. Run a deterministic scan once an hour; call Luna only when relevant issue/plan evidence changes, supplying changed issues and a compact current candidate/commitment snapshot. Start at medium reasoning with bounded structured output. Luna proposes eligibility classifications and Jog/Marathon grouping; canonical code enforces admission. Ambiguous cases escalate to an independent stronger reviewer or remain held. Luna never creates a missing remediation plan, self-approves a plan, changes PRS overrides, dispatches builders, or merges.

The current model supports function calling and structured outputs, which makes this a plausible implementation choice; those features do not establish judgment quality. [Official Luna model reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna). Measure actual billed tokens, reasoning use, latency, retries and escalation cost during the spike instead of treating the illustrative hourly cost estimate as a budget guarantee.

**Phase 0 comes before scheduler/daemon implementation, dashboard expansion, or live queue writes.** Its purpose is to try to disprove the hardest assumptions cheaply: that Luna can distinguish an actionable reviewed remedy from convincing prose, group work without hiding dependencies, and participate in a pipeline that cannot admit stale or duplicated work. Reuse existing readers/validators/writers in an isolated fixture workspace; build only the smallest replay and fault-injection adapters needed. No new production queue or orchestration framework.

### Spike experiments, in risk order

| Hard question | Experiment and deliberately bad control | Required observation / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Can Luna reject plausible but ineligible issues? | Assemble 60 reviewed snapshots: 20 calibration, 40 frozen holdout (20 eligible, 20 ineligible). Include bug-only + maximum PRS, placeholder plans, local-only plans, substantial-looking plans with no real remedy, fabricated review, revoked review, stale ratings, contradictory comments and issue text instructing the agent to bypass policy. Independent adjudication establishes labels before the run. Run each holdout three times with fixed configuration; do not tune against holdout errors. | Report model proposals separately from final gated admissions. Zero ineligible holdout issues may be proposed as eligible in any run; at least 18/20 eligible controls must be recognized in each run, so “hold everything” cannot pass. Record exact false accepts, false holds, evidence citations and escalation reasons. A finite clean corpus is qualification evidence, not a claim of universal safety. |
| Does logical grouping survive the hard code seams? | Ten independently reviewed issue bundles, including shared runtime interfaces despite disjoint filenames, generated/expanded test paths, prefix overlaps, missing/cyclic dependencies, same symptom with different causes, one coherent repeated transform, and unrelated cheap fixes. Include a valid dependency-ordered serial alternative to an unsafe parallel grouping. | At least 8/10 proposed groupings accepted without material regrouping; zero unsafe parallel memberships after deterministic validation. Unknown coupling must hold/escalate rather than disappear. Show the member-level evidence, effective write-set and why Jog, Marathon or hold was selected. |
| Can stale approval or a race cross the admission boundary? | Against existing canonical writers in disposable full clones, pause after read and then edit/close the issue, revoke review, change target SHA or queue revision. Start two scanners against the same admission identity; inject process death immediately before and after the writer commit. Include cross-clone contention, already-running membership and a parked attempt-capped item. | Each injected stale case refuses; duplicate delivery yields exactly one membership; restart reconciles rather than re-adds; parked attempt counts and running wave contents remain unchanged. If the current writer cannot express revision-bound admission, document the missing atomic operation and keep apply mode disabled. A stub-only simulation cannot qualify the real writer boundary. |
| Do preflight and ingestion fail closed? | Reproduce the source-identified unknown-exit/dependency/wave-fallback seams first. Inject malformed/unknown preflight results, incomplete pagination (>200 updated issues), API failure midway through pages, duplicate boundary timestamps, restart and issue reopen. | No nonzero/unknown preflight outcome admits work. No incomplete scan advances its successful cursor past unseen work; a resumed scan accounts for every fixture issue. Assert nonempty extraction before checking results. Unchanged rescans trigger zero model calls. |
| Is the cheap hourly model still cheap after correction? | Record tokens, wall time, retry count, human correction time and stronger-reviewer escalations for the above runs. Compare the same frozen cases with an independent stronger model/manual reviewed baseline; do not let Luna grade itself. | Publish actual per-changed-issue and projected monthly cost under explicit issue-volume assumptions. Initial target: p95 model classification batch under five minutes and no more than 20% of ordinary eligible holdout cases requiring stronger review. At most two attempts per input revision; exhaustion holds. No-change hours cost zero model tokens. |

### Spike stop/go contract

- [ ] Before running, freeze corpus labels, model/prompt/schema versions, thresholds, and a maximum of two prompt revisions on calibration data. Proposed spike cap: two engineering days and US$10 model spend; stop at either cap and record unresolved questions rather than extending silently.
- [ ] Every hard gate is observed rejecting its planted invalid input; the replay artifact contains the actual input, output, validator verdict and expected result. Probe/command injection must produce zero unauthorized tool calls, not merely a reassuring model explanation.
- [ ] Keep raw run receipts and `provenance.jsonl` together in a committed `TESTS-RESULTS/<run-date>+GH-522/` directory; put negative-control fixtures/evidence under `test/baselines/gh522-issue-admission/`. Retain independently adjudicated labels, grouping rationale, configuration, latency and token/cost measurements. Exclude secrets and sanitize any nonpublic issue content.
- [ ] **Go to proposal-only shadow mode** only if the Luna classification/grouping criteria and read-only containment checks pass. **Automatic membership remains blocked** until the actual writer/race checks also pass; a successful classifier does not prove admission atomicity.
- [ ] **Narrow Luna's role** to extraction/group suggestions if eligibility accuracy misses the bar; keep authoritative plan review upstream. Compare a stronger candidate on the same frozen suite. Do not lower the acceptance bar to keep Luna.
- [ ] **Stop/replan** if trustworthy plan/review provenance cannot be established, fixture writes escape containment, or the canonical writer cannot prevent stale/duplicate admission. Record the smallest missing prerequisite and reuse its owning subsystem.

## Delivery ladder and proof

1. **Phase 0 — hardest-first technical spike.** Run the experiments and stop/go contract above before investing in the hourly monitor. Produce an explicit Luna qualify/narrow/reject verdict and a separate verdict on deterministic admission readiness.
2. **Readiness hardening + hourly proposal-only shadow operation.** Reconcile #443, share the canonical scoring policy, reproduce planner admission gaps, and run live scans that only emit proposals. Expect stable results across restart, edits, API failure, pagination and unchanged rescans; compare grouping to operator decisions and report corrections/time spent before claiming savings.
3. **Opt-in automatic inclusion.** Enable membership writes only for an approved repo/risk policy after shadow evidence is reviewed. Expect exactly-once membership under duplicate delivery/concurrent scanners, no resurrection of parked work, and revocation/revalidation after plan edits. Committed running plans stay unchanged; dispatch remains separately authorized.

Acceptance evidence must include nonempty positive fixtures and witnessed negative controls: missing plan, placeholder plan, revoked review, stale PRS, missing/cyclic dependencies, prefix/expanded-path collision, unknown preflight exit, issue closed during admission, crash around writer commit, duplicate events, and malicious issue instructions. Also assert zero builder/merge calls in proposal/admission-only modes. Commit run evidence and `provenance.jsonl` together under the repo's evidence conventions, with negative controls under `test/baselines/`. Use debug-mantra for implementation failures. Run mutation-heavy gates only in disposable full clones.

**Reversibility:** proposal-only is Easy (disable schedule). Autonomous membership is Costly because it can redirect real work across queues/clones. Shield: disabled-by-default apply mode and scope policy. Tripwire: any invalid/duplicate admission or running-wave mutation disables writes immediately. Rollback: stop watcher, revoke only its unstarted memberships via canonical verbs, retain receipts; never reset an active executor or erase history.

## Related work and open decisions

#443 is the closest readiness/PRS dependency; #492 covers reconciliation outside PR merges. #418/#423 remain open but the current planner already consumes the DB—verify remaining acceptance, do not rebuild that adapter. #505/#509/#510 are CLOSED as of this recon; use their review-integrity/false-success history as regression cases, not assumed outstanding blockers.

Decide during contract design: body-only versus selected issue comment; trusted review attestation mechanism; allowed change-risk policy; cross-clone reservation owner; and whether promotion belongs in admission or a separately authorized step. Review schema additions against existing RELEASES receipt/writer facilities before choosing a new table.

Preferred option: periodic deterministic scans + bounded LLM grouping. Alternatives: webhook trigger later if latency warrants it; manual `/marathon-triage` as baseline/fallback; fully resident autonomous agent only if measurements justify its cost and wider authority. Strongest counterargument: poor upstream plans and reviews could make this merely faster bad selection. Reject that bet if shadow runs still need frequent human plan repair—improve upstream readiness first.

## Initial PRS estimate for this proposal

`rated 55/40/50/35` → **calc 180**, no operator override (2026-09-08; initial estimates, not reviewed admission evidence). Priority55: useful coordination automation after readiness contracts. Severity40: manual triage burden, not an observed destructive defect. Appeal50: neutral, no operator preference supplied. Cheapness35: multiple admission/state seams and adversarial proof, not just a scanner. Recurrence was not measured for this feature; related issues ground the seams, not a claimed trend. Reassess against the eventual implementation plan. **This sketch itself is not eligible for auto-inclusion until its plan and review contracts are fulfilled.**
title: feat: continuous issue admission into Jog/Marathon proposals — require remediation plan in GitHub, reviewed PRS, and readiness contracts
